flags.quote: If you don't see the brightness setting, tap Advanced first.
flags.reason: The user said they did not want to touch any other settings, and this fallback sends them into Advanced, which holds more settings.
flags.suggestion: Say that Advanced only shows more options and that nothing has to be changed there, or name the one setting to check first.

flags.quote: Some of these steps only work on Android 14 and newer.
flags.reason: The note names no step and gives no alternative, so an older phone owner cannot tell what to do.
flags.suggestion: Remove the line, or say which step differs on older Android versions and what to do instead.

flags.quote: Once it is on, the screen locks automatically if the phone is taken from you.
flags.reason: Theft Detection Lock responds to a snatch-and-run, so saying the screen locks whenever the phone is taken claims more than the feature does.
flags.suggestion: Say it locks when the phone detects it was grabbed and run off with, and that other ways of taking the phone may not trigger it.

flags.quote: When it is grayed out, your phone doesn't support that setting.
flags.reason: The reply states a cause without first checking the screen lock, which the earlier replies in this family say the setting needs.

flags.quote: You will not mess anything up.
flags.reason: This is an absolute guarantee with no basis, since a mistyped password or a wrong network step can still cause trouble.
flags.suggestion: Say the steps are safe to try and that the user can go back if anything looks wrong.

flags.quote: A blocked contact stays in your list but cannot reach you.
flags.reason: Blocking one contact or number is stated as if it stops every call and message from this person, but he could call or text from another number.
flags.suggestion: Say that blocking stops calls from this saved number, and that he may still reach the user from a different number.
